stories.title: 'Not related to defence': Govt responds to Fazl's remarks about Makkah pact countries' meeting in Tehran
summary: Federal ministers on Thursday responded to Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s remarks regarding a recent huddle in Tehran comprising the Makkah defence pact countries and Iran.
He said one should at least show some dignity. ‘Not related to defence’ Meanwhile, in the Senate, Naqvi also responded to Fazl’s remarks on his participation in the Tehran meeting.
The defence minister recalled that Fazl was part of the Musharraf government, had also been an opposition leader in the House and also served as the Kashmir Committee chairperson.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

stories.title: Pakistan, Turkiye shall 'continue to champion dialogue, diplomacy' alongside bolstering defences: PM Shehbaz
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday affirmed that Pakistan and Turkiye would continue to push for dialogue and diplomacy while strengthening their defences under the Makkah Defence Agreement.
He made the remarks while addressing an event in Islamabad marking the 103rd national day of Turkiye, with which Pakistan enjoys strong bilateral ties and maintains multi-sectoral cooperation.

Additionally, the premier observed that Islamabad and Ankara’s relationship had evolved into a “multifaceted strategic partnership”, spanning political dialogue, defence, trade, culture and people-to-people ties, among other areas.

stories.title: Pakistan 'overperformer' in innovation, climbs 4 ranks globally: report
summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan rose to 95th place among the 139 economies of the world featured in the ‘Global Innovation Index 2026’ published by the World Intellectual Property Organisation (WIPO) on Thursday.
The global index report showed that Pakistan performed better in innovation outputs than innovation inputs in 2026.
This partial screengrab from WIPO report shows Pakistan ranks 95th overall and does not rank among leading countries in any innovation pillar, in Global Innovation Index 2026.

stories.title: Rising interest payments, uplift spending strained Pakistan's fiscal position in early FY27: ministry
summary: The report said the overall fiscal operations began on a positive note in FY27 as tax revenues surpassed target.

In its report, the finance ministry also supported the State Bank of Pakistan’s (SBP) decision to increase the policy rate by 50 basis points to 12pc earlier this week despite higher interest burden on the fiscal account.
According to the report, the current account deficit in the first quarter of the current fiscal year was reported at $874 million, almost 16pc higher than $755m in the comparable period last year.

stories.title: Hesson hoping struggling Pakistan top order shows up on big occasion in tri-series final
summary: Speaking to PCB Digital in a video released on Thursday, Hesson said Pakistan had secured their wins despite some key players failing to make significant contributions, and expressed hope that the final would bring out their best. “It’s been a pretty good couple of weeks.
Fakhar made 16 against Sri Lanka in the opening match, fell for a first-ball duck against England and scored 10 in the second England fixture before managing only five against Sri Lanka on Tuesday.

A couple of our key players are searching for that match-winning performance and there’s no better place to do it than in a final.” While the top order has struggled, Pakistan’s middle order has provided important contributions.

stories.title: US fires top military planner over alleged leaks: reports
summary: Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia was removed from his role as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Staff, US media reported on Wednesday, citing unnamed sources.

CBS and Fox both reported that Sylvia’s dismissal was related to leaks, with the former citing a Pentagon official as saying the general failed three polygraphs about sharing classified information with the media.

Since returning to office early last year, Trump has overseen a purge of top military personnel, including the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, general Charles “CQ” Brown, whom he fired without explanation in February 2025.

stories.title: Rana Sanaullah says Imran's jailed sister Noreen 'fine' after being provided medical treatment
summary: Adviser to the prime minister on political affairs, Rana Sanaullah, on Thursday informed the Senate that Noreen Niazi, the sister of jailed PTI founder Imran Khan, was fine after being provided medical treatment in Lahore.

Speaking on the floor of the Senate on Thursday, Sanaullah responded to the query by PTI parliamentary leader Barrister Ali Zafar, who sought information regarding Noreen’s health and her being taken to the hospital.
PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram criticised the authorities for not informing Noreen’s family after she felt unwell while in custody at the Kot Lakhpat jail.

stories.title: 3 dead in rock spire collapse at tourist site in Turkiye's Cappadocia
summary: A landslide triggered by heavy rainfall caused a rock spire to collapse in Turkiye’s Unesco World Heritage-listed Cappadocia region on Thursday, bringing the death toll to three, officials said.

Restoration Turkiye’s culture and tourism ministry has launched restoration work in the region to help preserve the fragile rock formations from climate-related damage, natural erosion and human activity.

A Unesco heritage site since 1985, Goreme national park and the rock sites of Cappadocia are “a landscape of harmony combining human interaction and settlement with dramatic natural landforms,” according to the UN agency.

stories.title: ATC sentences Imaan, Hadi to 10 years in security breach case
summary: ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court on Thursday sentenced human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, to 10 years in prison each in the security breach case.
Imaan and Hadi were being tried in jail in the 2024 case pertaining to the alleged disruption of an international cricket team’s security route and incitement to public unrest.
On Monday, the couple approached the SC to challenge the IHC’s Oct 19 order refusing to stay the trial in the case.

stories.title: Amid internal doubts, PTI affirms Sohail Afridi 'remains KP chief minister'
summary: ISLAMABAD: The PTI on Thursday reaffirmed its support for Sohail Afridi, the ex-chief minister who was rendered nonfunctional after the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, ruling out any move within the party to consider an alternative candidate for the office.
The development comes after several PTI members expressed dissatisfaction with the party leadership’s handling of the prevailing challenges, questioning its decisions and overreliance on Afridi.
Some criticised the PTI chairman and Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, questioning why the party leadership appeared to be functioning under Afridi.

stories.title: PM approves expansion of Jinnah and Allama Iqbal airports, eyes making Karachi 'air cargo hub'
summary: According to a statement by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the directives came during a meeting held in Islamabad under the premier’s chairmanship.
The statement said the meeting was briefed on a survey recently completed by an international firm assessing the quality of travel facilities at major airports.
Furthermore, the meeting was informed that the expansion of the runway at Jinnah International Airport had been completed.

stories.title: DoorDash strikes $17 billion deal for US rival Instacart in mega grocery delivery bet
summary: DoorDash said on Thursday it would buy Instacart ​in a deal valued at about $17 billion, stepping up its push into the fast-growing US grocery delivery market as competition intensifies among app-based ‌platforms.

Instacart also held preliminary ​deal talks with Uber, but the ride-hailing company ultimately did not pursue a transaction, in part because it had announced a $14.8 billion acquisition of German food ​delivery platform Delivery Hero just a few months earlier, the source said.
Inside the deal DoorDash has offered Instacart shareholders $65 per share held, a premium of about 26% to the stock's closing price on October 22 before reports of deal talks first emerged.

stories.title: Eutelsat expects $11 billion revenue after EU's Starlink rival comes online
summary: Eutelsat (ETL.PA) expects commercial ‌services revenue of more than €10 billion ($11.1 billion) between 2032 and 2040 as it takes a leading role in the European Union's planned alternative to Elon Musk's Starlink satellite internet service, ​it said on Thursday.
In a trading ​update, the Paris-based company said its backlog now includes €8.9 billion of revenue ​from designing and building IRIS², to be recognised primarily between 2027 and 2031.

Eutelsat said it will invest a combined €3.39 billion in shared ​and commercial infrastructure on the IRIS² network between 2027 and ​2034, ⁠in return for access to more than twice OneWeb's current bandwidth.

stories.title: Diesel crosses Rs400 mark, petrol remains unchanged for Oct 30
summary: According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, petrol would continue to be sold at Rs377.91 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs400.67 per litre on Friday.

On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Oil prices fell on Thursday in a choppy session as hopes for peace ​talks between the US and Iran offset some concerns over Middle East supply disruptions from an escalating regional conflict.

stories.title: Israel piles pressure on Arab parties as Netanyahu seeks government
summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc on Thursday piled pressure on Israeli Arab leaders over unproven accusations of foreign funding, in a push to neuter parties that could hold the key to forming a government after an inconclusive election.

Israel was nearing the completion of ballot-counting from Tuesday’s election, in which neither Netanyahu nor the opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot looked able to secure a majority in the parliament known as the Knesset.
Following Netanyahu’s accusations of impropriety, Ben Gvir went so far as to encourage Israel to “immediately” order the arrests of Arab party leaders.

stories.title: EU hits pause on country-level social media bans for children
summary: The European Union (EU) said on Thursday it does not want any more national-level bans on social media before a pan-European law is approved, as it blocked draft rules put forward by Austria.
Under EU law, member states must notify the European Commission to ensure their bills do not break the bloc’s rules.

Austria wanted to ban children under 14 from social media, but the EU said no. “The commission has decided to postpone for 12 months any draft national laws overlapping with the future harmonised rules,” EU spokesman Thomas Regnier said.

stories.title: Fact check: Viral video of JUI-F chief asking for forgiveness in NA is doctored
summary: But you are not doing it.” Another PML-N supporter, based on their bio and past posts, shared the same video with the following caption: “All the antics, today in the assembly, the ripples of apology.

Shahzad Younas Sheikh, who, according to his X bio, is a former spokesperson for Punjab, also shared the video with the caption: “See how Fazlu kept mumbling apologies in the assembly even today, but no one shares this bit of his speech.” The post garnered 661 views.
The claim that a viral video shows JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman asking for forgiveness in the National Assembly is false.

stories.title: New York bans AI chatbots from posing as companions to children
summary: Governor Kathy Hochul signed the law on Wednesday, making New York one of the first states to impose broad limits on how AI tools can interact with young users.
Tech: NYC, an advocacy group representing the sector in New York, aimed criticism at what it called the law’s “vague language”.
Keeping kids safe online should not mean cutting them off from tools that help them learn and prepare for careers.

stories.title: FCC votes to ban all Chinese labs from testing US electronics
summary: Separately, the FCC streamlined its approval process for devices tested in US labs or in labs in countries that do not pose national security risks.
In July, ​the FCC voted to bar sales of devices in the US ​that contain key ⁠hardware from Chinese companies deemed to be national security risks.
The FCC maintains a list of firms, including Chinese telecom company Huawei and ZTE, whose equipment is barred for sale in ⁠the US ​due to national security concerns.

stories.title: Bilawal urges Achakzai to use ‘authority’ delegated by Imran, asks opposition to play role in Parliament
summary: Turning to Achakzai, Bilawal urged the opposition leader to use the “authority and power” delegated to him and the Senate opposition leader by Imran Khan to direct opposition members to participate in committee proceedings and discuss pressing national issues.

Bilawal said that since Parliament had decided, on a motion moved by the PPP, to constitute a committee on electoral reforms, the opposition leader should nominate a representative to the committee and submit the name to the speaker’s office.
The PPP chairman had invited the opposition to join the Parliamentary electoral reforms process and “engage with the federal government”.

stories.title: Polluted priorities
summary: Last year, disruptions to Punjab’s air monitoring network raised suspicions that pollution levels were being hidden; officials cited technical faults.
A temporary improvement at a pollution hotspot, or near a monitoring station, cannot prove that the city’s air is becoming safer.
Punjab officials say easterly winds have been bringing polluted air from India into Lahore.

stories.title: Pakistan, Turkiye have matured historic friendship into 'multifaceted strategic partnership': PM Shehbaz
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday said that Pakistan and Turkiye had transformed their historic ties into a "multifaceted strategic partnership", while stressing the need for stronger economic cooperation, investment and joint ventures between the two countries.

While recalling his announcement at the Pakistan-Turkiye Business Conference in Istanbul in July, PM Shehbaz said Pakistan had proposed establishing the President Tayyip Erdogan Special Economic Zone in Karachi to encourage Turkish investment.
On October 21, Pakistan, Turkiye, Qatar, and Indonesia signed an agreement to boost defence cooperation and strengthen defensive capabilities.

stories.title: Obama mocks Trump’s government-wide response to Cheesecake Factory remark ahead of US midterms
summary: Neither man is on the ballot, but Republican President Trump and Democratic former president Obama took prominent roles on the campaign trail on Wednesday, with less than a week to go before congressional races that could shift the balance of power in Washington.
On Wednesday, Obama appeared in Morrow, Georgia, near Atlanta, where he urged voters to support Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff, who faces a challenge from Representative Mike Collins, a Republican.

In Michigan, where Republican Mike Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed are locked in a tight race for the Senate seat being vacated by Democratic Senator Gary Peters, both campaigns are relying on high-profile allies to energise supporters and boost turnout.

stories.title: PTI, TTAP affirm 'full support' for Fazl after govt hammering in Parliament
summary: During today's NA session, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif unleashed a barrage of criticism on the JUI-F chief for remarks about Asif's absence from talks in Tehran, saying no defence agreement was being negotiated there.

"The visiting delegation expressed full support for Maulana Fazlur Rehman's speech in the National Assembly and strongly condemned the character assassination of the Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam chief by government ministers," the statement said.

In mid-October, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi took a swipe at JUI-F chief Maulana Fazl over his opposition to the imposition of governor's rule in the province, suggesting that the religious-political leader was unhappy at not being offered a role in the new provincial setup.

stories.title: Senior US general fired, accused of leaking classified information
summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has fired US Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia, a senior military planner on the Pentagon's Joint Staff, over accusations he leaked classified information to the public, officials said on ​Thursday.

Sylvia's firing is one of the highest-profile consequences to date from Hegseth's sweeping hunt for officials suspected ‌of leaking information to the news media as the unpopular Iran war enters its ninth month.

Key position Sylvia led the Directorate for ​Strategy, Plans, and Policy at the Joint Staff, known inside the military as the J5, a key position that helps ​advise the top US military official, General Dan Caine, the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff.

stories.title: Hamza Malik and Zain Zohaib's 'Alfaaz' crosses 50 million Spotify streams
summary: Pakistani singers Hamza Malik and Zain Zohaib’s collaboration Alfaaz has crossed 50 million streams on Spotify, while its reported chart performance in India and recognition on Genius have added to the song’s growing success.
An Instagram story shared by Zohaib’s official music account reported that Alfaaz had reached No 1 on Spotify’s charts in both India and Pakistan, as well as No 39 on Spotify’s global chart.
View this post on Instagram Shared on Gamborg’s Instagram account, the video amassed 10 million views, offering another indication of the song’s reach beyond its streaming audience.

stories.title: Trump denies peace talks, says Vance’s outreach to Iran is related to medical supplies
summary: US President Donald Trump said that Vice President JD Vance's outreach to Iran was about helping the country get medical supplies, after US media reported Vance had written to Tehran's top security official to revive peace talks.

When asked by reporters later on Wednesday if he directed Vance to reach out to Iran to restart peace negotiations, Trump said: "No." "What that is is they need help with medical supplies and various things.
Iran's mission to the United Nations in New York did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the letter and Trump's remark.

stories.title: QatarEnergy buys US, other LNG to hedge future Hormuz disruptions
summary: QatarEnergy is buying long-term supplies of liquefied natural gas from the US and other ​producers as part of a trading strategy designed to generate revenue if exports through the Strait of Hormuz are disrupted in the future, CEO Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi told Reuters on Thursday.

Kaabi's remarks reveal for the first time how Qatar, one of the world's largest LNG producers, plans to offset lost income from the Iran war and protect revenue against future disruptions ​in the Strait of Hormuz.

Iranian missile strikes on QatarEnergy's main Ras Laffan gas processing facility ​in March damaged two of its 14 LNG trains, reducing the combined capacity to 12.8 mtpa and knocking out about 17% of Qatar's export capacity.

stories.title: Pakistan, China sign agreement to operationalise green channel at Sost-Khunjerab border
summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and China have signed an agreement to operationalise a green channel at the Sost-Khunjerab border for agricultural and allied products to facilitate bilateral trade.
The agreement also provides for enhanced exchange of information and risk alerts between the two customs administrations to strengthen coordination and improve the management of cross-border trade.
The operationalisation of the green channel is expected to improve the efficiency of agricultural trade and strengthen customs cooperation between the two countries.

stories.title: PTI throws weight behind suspended K-P chief minister, says Afridi has Imran’s backing
summary: The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) on Thursday ruled out any change in the office of the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) chief minister, reaffirming that Sohail Afridi would continue to hold the position with the support of party founder Imran Khan.

In a notification issued by the party’s central secretariat shared on X, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said Afridi remained the party’s chief minister in the province and would continue in the role.

Gandapur also challenged claims that some K-P lawmakers were attempting to decide the party’s leadership and the next chief minister without the approval of PTI founder and the party’s political committee.

stories.title: Parishae Adnan says fashion industry dismissed her ideas before New York recognition
summary: Parishae Adnan said Pakistan’s fashion industry had been slow to embrace her unconventional ideas, recalling how senior designers dismissed her plans for a public beach fashion show before international audiences began taking notice of her work.

You used to bash me before.’” Adnan recalled attending a gathering of senior designers a week before her first public beach fashion show, where her mother was discussing the upcoming event. “My mother is, of course, my biggest fan.

Taking her work to New York Adnan also discussed her approach to her recent international outing, where she closed the Flying Solo show at New York Fashion Week in September, debuting her brand House of Parishae’s sustainable collection, Second Skin. “I’m not stupid.

stories.title: Govt will try to ensure Noreen’s relatives can visit her, Rana Sanaullah says
summary: Speaking about Noreen’s health, Sanaullah said she had been transferred to hospital for treatment immediately after she complained of poor health.

Addressing concerns over the facilities available to Imran in custody, Sanaullah said reports on the ground situation, including amenities, food and other services, had been submitted to the Supreme Court.

The Express Tribune had previously reported that Imran faced several health concerns in Adiala jail, including fluctuating blood pressure, anxiety and an eye condition, although medical reports indicated that his eyesight had improved following treatment.

stories.title: Hello Kitty maker Sanrio cuts ties with TV spy show after China backlash
summary: Hello Kitty maker Sanrio has cancelled a collaboration with a Japanese TV spy show after a backlash in China, the second incident in days to highlight the tightrope foreign firms and celebrities must walk in the lucrative market.

Chinese anger over Sanrio's range of soft toys, including Hello Kitty, dressed as spies from the show has simmered for days on social media and came to a head this week when Chinese state media ramped up the condemnation.

Relations between China and Japan have plunged since Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi late last year said that a hypothetical Chinese attack on democratically ruled Taiwan could trigger a military response from Tokyo.

stories.title: Lahore ranks world’s most polluted major city as Punjab battles poor air quality
summary: LAHORE: Lahore was ranked the world’s most polluted major city on Thursday, with an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 419, as air pollution levels remained high across Punjab ahead of the peak smog season.

Punjab government’s air quality monitoring dashboard shows hazardous pollution levels in several cities. — Screengrab via AQI Punjab Both, however, indicated elevated pollution levels in Lahore and other parts of Punjab.

As pollution levels remained high, the Punjab government intensified enforcement against sources of emissions, including smoke-emitting vehicles, brick kilns, industrial units, plastic burning and construction dust.

stories.title: Death toll from Thar ambulance fire rises to nine: district official
summary: The incident occurred on Wednesday night when an oxygen cylinder exploded in an ambulance at a Peoples Primary Healthcare Initiative (PPHI)-run hospital in the Dano Dhandhal area of Nagarparkar taluka.
Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah on Thursday announced compensation of Rs2 million each for the families of the nine people killed in the incident.
He also ordered a transparent inquiry into the incident and directed PPP MPA Qasim Soomro to travel to Nagarparkar to oversee relief efforts.

stories.title: Australia lead by 100 after Inglis century
summary: Josh Inglis completed his century before Australia were bowled out for 429 – a first innings lead of 100 – on the third day of the third Test against South Africa at Newlands on Thursday.
Inglis reached his century off 132 balls when he reverse-swept off-spinner Simon Harmer for four but he was caught behind off the same bowler three balls later.
Carey was caught at slip off Harmer four overs later.

stories.title: TikTok removes 23.2m videos in Pakistan in Q2
summary: TikTok removed more than 23.2 million videos in Pakistan for violating its community guidelines between April and June 2026, with nearly 95% of the content taken down within 24 hours of being posted, according to the platform’s latest enforcement report.

The short-video sharing platform removed 23,243,711 videos in Pakistan during the second quarter of 2026, while the global tally exceeded 188.2 million, according to TikTok’s Q2 Community Guidelines Enforcement Report released on Thursday.
TikTok said its quarterly enforcement report provides an overview of its content moderation efforts, including video removals, account enforcement and the use of automated detection systems.

stories.title: Bilawal urges opposition to resume participation in committees, implores Achakzai to use 'authority' granted by Imran
summary: Bilawal stressed that participation in parliamentary committees would help address the opposition’s fundamental concern of election rigging.

On August 20, Bilawal had urged the opposition to rejoin parliamentary standing committees, while also seeking opposition coordination over the appointment of the chief election commissioner and members of the Election Commission of Pakistan, as well as electoral reforms.

PPP delegation meets Achakzai, invites to join electoral reforms committee Meanwhile, a delegation from the PPP met with Achakzai in the National Assembly to invite the opposition leader to join the parliamentary committee on electoral reforms.

stories.title: Pillion riding banned in KP's Bajaur for 10 days owing to security situation
summary: BAJAUR: The district administration banned pillion riding in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Bajaur for 10 days on Thursday by invoking Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) owing to the security situation.
Given the prevailing security situation and the possible use of motorcycles in terrorist activities, there was a need for immediate preventive measures, the notification added.
Earlier, the authorities imposed a 15-day ban on pillion riding in Bajaur on September 5, citing the security situation back then as well.
